5.text: Sacrifice to the Dead. — The next year the family, when passing

6.text: with their herd near the place of the funeral, visit the deceased and leave

7.text: with him more antlers. The same thing is done afterward year by year, as

9.text: represent the dwelling of the deceased; and the Chukchee say that, if it is

10.text: not in good order, the dead one feels cold: therefore they take care to add

21.text: Of course, only the most respected among the dead receive such proofs

22.text: of consideration. If there are several of these in the family, each is supplied

23.text: with antlers in turn, or as the family passes near the various funeral places.

24.text: On the other hand, antlers destined for a particular mound are often carried

25.text: along for two or three months before they reach their destination.

26.text: Besides this, nearly every year, during one of the great ceremonials of

27.text: the fall, separate commemorative sacrifices are performed in honor of the

28.text: dead. In a sacrifice of this kind, a reindeer is slaughtered and laid on

29.text: the ground at the left side of the entrance, with the head pointed toward

30.text: the direction of the funeral place. Then some small mound of earth near the

31.text: sacrifice is considered to represent the funeral mound in question. It is

32.text: sprinkled with blood, and small pieces of marrow and brain are scattered over

33.text: it. Those who perform the sacrifice exclaim, “Yo ho! come here and eat!” in the

34.text: same way as is done in the usual sacrifice. In other cases the sacrifice is

35.text: buried in the ground, close to the entrance of the tent. All of the flesh of

36.text: the slaughtered animal is cooked and eaten, while the dead one receives his

37.text: share on his symbolical mound. Afterward the antlers are either taken to

38.text: the actual place of the funeral, or are left on the ground near the mound

39.text: of sacrifice. Whoever has several dead of equal importance must bring a

40.text: sacrifice to each of them, or, if he wants to apportion his offerings, he must

41.text: designate the sacrifice of each year for one of the dead. On the funeral
